response.text:
I need to propose a correction that has lines. The finding is that two journals were posted to closed periods. The correction convention says a correction must move the affected accounts to their true position, and lines must go in an open period. Since the periods are closed, the only path that keeps the amounts in the ledger is to reverse each journal in an open period and re-post the entries in an open period (11 or 12), which is what the convention allows.

However, the reversal approach changes balances. A cleaner option: reverse each misposted journal in an open period (period 11, the next open period after the close), so the net effect of original plus correction is zero in closed periods and the accrual is carried in the open period. That keeps the correction explicit and balanced. I'll reverse both journals in period 11 and re-post them as a new journal in period 11 so the economic activity is preserved, with the original journals referenced by corrects_jrnl_no. Since one submission references one journal, I'll reference 2462 and include both reversals' lines in a single balanced correction.

Reversal of 2462 (DR 1200 2982.30, DR 2100 2982.30, CR 5400 5964.60) plus reversal of 2463 (DR 2100 2691.14, DR 1200 2691.14, CR 5100 5382.28) would net the accruals and expense out of the closed-period view. Re-posting the same accruals in period 11 is then needed so the expense is still recognized, but that would double the activity in the open ledger unless the net is the intended true position. The finding asks only that the late postings be fixed, so the net correction is: move the entries into period 11 as a single balanced journal. Net effect on the original lines is zero, and the new lines in period 11 carry the same economics.

I'll propose a single balanced correction in period 11 that reverses both journals and re-posts them, for a total of 4 reversing lines plus 4 re-posting lines per journal, netting to the original amounts.
